hero.h1: Assay: mock technical interviews built around your weak spots
hero.label: Highlights

one.title: Assay your skills before the interview does.
one.body: Pick your stack or paste a job post. Assay builds a mock interview around your weak spots: quizzes, live coding and a graded report.

two.title: Paste a job link. Get that exact interview.
two.body: Djinni, DOU or Glassdoor: we read the post, find the skills and test you on precisely those. On-device AI keeps the text in your browser.

how.title: From job post to graded interview in four steps
how.intro: Assay works like an assayer's lab: we take a sample of what the job demands, test your skills against it and tell you exactly how pure the result is.

one.title: Choose the ore
one.body: Pick skills from the catalogue, paste a job link or drop in the description text.

two.title: We assay the post
two.body: A keyword parser or an on-device language model extracts the skills and seniority.

three.title: Take the interview
three.body: Quizzes and coding tasks aimed at your weakest skills, with a lecture one click away.

four.title: Read your grade
four.body: Every answer next to the correct one, a karat grade and what to train next.

map.title: A map of everything an interviewer can ask
map.body: Assay tracks your mastery per skill. Every new interview leans into the areas you haven't proven yet, and skips what you've already nailed.
map.legend: Skill categories, sized by the number of skills we recognise

lectures.empty: Lectures will appear here once the content is seeded.

free.a: Yes. Sign in with Google and practise as much as you like.

ai.q: How does the on-device AI work?
ai.a: Your browser downloads a compact language model once (about 1 GB) and runs it on your GPU through WebGPU. The job description is analysed on your device and is never sent to an AI provider.

sites.a: Djinni, DOU and most sites that publish structured job postings. Glassdoor often blocks automated reads. If that happens, paste the description instead.

grade.a: Each task is weighted by its complexity. Opening a lecture for help keeps 85% of the credit. Your percentage maps to a karat grade, from Raw ore up to 24K.

coding.q: What do I need for the coding tasks?
coding.a: Only a modern browser. The coding grounds run TypeScript, JavaScript, React and Angular in a sandbox with an instant preview and automatic tests.

adaptive.q: How does Assay choose my tasks?
adaptive.a: It estimates your mastery of every skill from past attempts, gives more questions to weaker skills, retries tasks you failed and avoids ones you passed recently.

tips.one: Interviewers value thinking out loud more than instant answers.
tips.two: State the time and space complexity before you're asked.
tips.three: Clarify edge cases first: empty input, duplicates, very large values.
tips.four: If you get stuck, explain what you'd try next. That's half the answer.
tips.five: Tests in the coding grounds run automatically after every change.
